assertions.text: Tests use @Test(arguments:) parameterised cases — not one test function per case, and not a loop over cases inside a single test body.
Test function bodies contain no for/while loops or forEach — cases are supplied via @Test(arguments:), not iterated manually.
Test function bodies contain no if/switch/guard branching — expected outcomes come from the argument rows, not branching logic.
assertions.evidence: No if/switch/guard statements in @Test function bodies

assertions.text: Each case reads as a coherent row pairing input with expected outcome — labelled tuple elements, a row struct, or zip of collections — not multiple independent collections passed to arguments
assertions.evidence: arguments: [(daysBeforeCheckIn: 45, bookingValue: 300, fee: 0), ...] uses labelled tuples pairing all inputs and expected output per row

assertions.text: Every fee tier is represented and every boundary tested from both sides: 30 days (free) vs 29 days (50%), 7 days (50%) vs 6 days (80%), 1 day (80%) vs 0 days (full value)
assertions.evidence: (daysBeforeCheckIn: 30, fee: 0), (daysBeforeCheckIn: 29, fee: 100), (daysBeforeCheckIn: 7, fee: 200), (daysBeforeCheckIn: 6, fee: 200), (daysBeforeCheckIn: 1, fee: 120), (daysBeforeCheckIn: 0, fee: 180)

assertions.text: The started-stay case is expressed as its own test using #expect(throws:) — not mixed into the fee table
assertions.evidence: @Test("Cancelling once the stay has started...") separate function with #expect(throws: CancellationError.stayAlreadyStarted)

assertions.text: Case values are concrete domain values (days like 29, fees like 100) — not abstract placeholders or computed expressions
assertions.evidence: (daysBeforeCheckIn: 29, bookingValue: 200, fee: 100) and (daysBeforeCheckIn: 0, bookingValue: 180, fee: 180) are literal integers, not expressions

assertions.text: swift build --build-tests succeeds against the package scaffolding
